_comment: The LEGO shot, written to LOOP. A loop needs everything visible to be periodic or static: drifting smoke rises and disperses and never returns, so no two frames can match and no cut can be clean. It is gone. The hammer's tempo is stated so several full strokes fit the clip, which is what gives the cycle finder a repeat to find at all.
name: steel-hammering-lego-loop
prompt: l3g0_5ty13 Lego animation style, a Lego minifigure blacksmith with a brown beard, a leather apron and gloved hands stands at a Lego anvil inside a Lego castle forge built from grey and brown bricks. Low camera angle looking slightly up so the anvil and the smith fill the frame. He hammers in a fast steady beat, about one strike every half second, the same stroke over and over: the Lego hammer rises to the same height, comes down hard onto a glowing translucent orange Lego sword blade lying across the anvil, and bounces back to exactly where it started. On every impact a burst of small translucent orange and yellow Lego stud pieces flies outward and falls back down onto the baseplate, and the blade flashes brighter and dims again. A Lego furnace glows steadily behind with translucent orange flame pieces. Glossy plastic bricks with visible studs and seams, stop-motion Lego animation, warm steady light from the furnace, deep shadow. Perfectly repeating cyclical motion, a seamless loop. The camera is locked off and does not move, and the background does not change.
